# [Flashcards](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#flashcards "Permanent link")

## [Creating](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#creating "Permanent link")

[Piotr Wozniak's 20 rules of knowledge formulation](https://supermemo.guru/wiki/20_rules_of_knowledge_formulation) is a great introduction on proper flashcard creation.

### Single-line Basic (Remnote style)[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#single-line-basic-remnote-style "Permanent link")

The prompt and the answer are separated by `::` (this can be configured in settings).

`the question goes on this side::the answer on this side`

### Single-line Reversed[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#single-line-reversed "Permanent link")

Creates two cards `side1:::side2` & the reversed version `side2:::side1`.

The prompt and the answer are separated by `:::` (this can be configured in settings).

`the question goes on this side:::the answer on this side!`

Note: In the first review, the plugin will show non-reversed card and reversed card. If **Bury sibling cards until the next day?** turn on, only non-reversed card will appear.

### Multi-line Basic[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#multi-line-basic "Permanent link")

The front and the back of the card are separated by `?` (this can be configured in settings).

````
Front of multiline
?
Backside of multiline card
````

These can also span over multiple lines as long as both sides "touch" the `?`:

````
As per the definition
of "multiline" the prompt
can be on multiple lines
?
same goes for
the answer
````

### Multi-line Reversed[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#multi-line-reversed "Permanent link")

Creates two cards `side1??side2` & the reversed version `side2??side1`.

The front and the back of the card are separated by `??` (this can be configured in settings).

````
Front of multiline
??
Backside of multiline card
````

These can also span over multiple lines as long as both sides "touch" the `??`:

````
As per the definition
of "multiline" the prompt
can be on multiple lines
??
same goes for
the answer
````

Note: The behavior is the same as single line reversed.

### Cloze cards[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#cloze-cards "Permanent link")

You can easily add cloze deletion cards using `==highlights==`, `**bolded text**`, or `{{text in curly braces}}`.

These can be turned on or off in settings.

Anki style `{{c1:This text}} would {{c2:generate}} {{c1:2 cards}}` cloze deletions are not currently supported. This feature is being tracked [here](https://github.com/st3v3nmw/obsidian-spaced-repetition/issues/93/).

## Decks[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#decks "Permanent link")

![Screenshot from 2021-06-05 19-28-24](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/43380836/120922211-78603400-c6d0-11eb-9d09-bdd5df1c9112.png)

The green and blue counts on the right of each deck name represent due and new cards respectively.

### Using Obsidian Tags[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#using-obsidian-tags "Permanent link")

1. Specify flashcard tags in settings (`#flashcards` is the default).
2. Tag any notes that you'd like to put flashcards using said tags.

#### Hierarchical Tags[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#hierarchical-tags "Permanent link")

Note that `#flashcards` will match nested tags like `#flashcards/subdeck/subdeck`.

#### Multiple Tags Within a Single File[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#multiple-tags-within-a-single-file "Permanent link")

A single file can contain cards for multiple different decks.

This is possible because a tag pertains to all subsequent cards in a file until any subsequent tag.

For example:

````
#flashcards/deckA
Question1 (in deckA)::Answer1
Question2 (also in deckA)::Answer2
Question3 (also in deckA)::Answer3

#flashcards/deckB
Question4 (in deckB)::Answer4
Question5 (also in deckB)::Answer5

#flashcards/deckC
Question6 (in deckC)::Answer6
````

#### A Single Card Within Multiple Decks[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#a-single-card-within-multiple-decks "Permanent link")

Usually the content of a card is only relevant to a single deck. However, sometimes content doesn't fall neatly into a single deck of the hierarchy.

In these cases, a card can be tagged as being part of multiple decks. The following card is specified as being in the three different decks listed.

````
#flashcards/language/words #flashcards/trivia #flashcards/learned-from-tv
A group of cats is called a::clowder
````

Note that as shown in the above example, all tags must be placed on the same line, separated by spaces.

#### Question Specific Tags[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#question-specific-tags "Permanent link")

A tag that is present at the start of the first line of a card is "question specific", and applies only to that card.

For example:

```
#flashcards/deckA
Question1 (in deckA)::Answer1
Question2 (also in deckA)::Answer2
Question3 (also in deckA)::Answer3

#flashcards/deckB Question4 (in deckB)::Answer4

Question6 (in deckA)::Answer6
```

Here `Question6` will be part of `deckA` and not `deckB` as `deckB` is specific to `Question4` only.

### Using Folder Structure[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#using-folder-structure "Permanent link")

The plugin will automatically search for folders that contain flashcards & use their paths to create decks & sub-decks i.e. `Folder/sub-folder/sub-sub-folder` ⇔ `Deck/sub-deck/sub-sub-deck`.

This is an alternative to the tagging option and can be enabled in settings.

## Reviewing[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#reviewing "Permanent link")

Once done creating cards, click on the flashcards button on the left ribbon to start reviewing the flashcards. After a card is reviewed, a HTML comment is added containing the next review day, the interval, and the card's ease.

````

````

Wrapping in a HTML comment makes the scheduling information not visible in the notes preview. For single-line cards, you can choose whether you want the HTML comment on the same line or on a separate line in the settings. Putting them on the same line prevents breaking of list structures in the preview or after auto-formatting.

Note that you can skip a card by simply pressing `S` (case doesn't matter).

Tip

If you're experiencing issues with the size of the modal on mobile devices, go to settings and set the _Flashcard Height Percentage_ and _Flashcard Width Percentage_ to 100% to maximize it.

### Faster Review[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#faster-review "Permanent link")

To review faster, use the following keyboard shortcuts:

- `Space/Enter` => Show answer
- `0` => Reset card's progress (Sorta like `Again` in Anki)
- `1` => Review as `Hard`
- `2` or `Space` => Review as `Good`
- `3` => Review as `Easy`

### Context[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#context "Permanent link")

If the parent note has heading(s), the flashcard will have a title containing the context.

Taking the following note:

````
#flashcards

# Trivia

## Capitals

### Africa

Kenya::Nairobi

### North America

Canada::Ottawa
````

The flashcard for `Kenya::Nairobi` will have `Trivia > Capitals > Africa` as the context/title whereas the flashcard for `Canada::Ottawa` will have `Trivia > Capitals > North America` as the context/title.

### Deleting cards[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#deleting-cards "Permanent link")

To delete a card, simply delete the scheduling information & the card text.

### Ignoring cards[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#ignoring-cards "Permanent link")

You can wrap flashcards in HTML comments e.g. `<!--Card text  -->` to prevent it from showing up in your review queues. You can always remove the wrapping comment later.

## Cramming[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#cramming "Permanent link")

Currently, the only supported method is "cramming" all cards in a note using the Cram flashcards in this note command. Will work on a per-deck across-all-notes method.

## Statistics[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#statistics "Permanent link")

The statistics section can be accessed using the `View Statistics` command.

### Forecast[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#forecast "Permanent link")

Stats on the number of cards due in the future.

![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/st3v3nmw/obsidian-spaced-repetition/master/assets/stats_forecast.png)

### Intervals[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#intervals "Permanent link")

Stats on delays until cards are shown again.

### Eases[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#eases "Permanent link")

Stats on card eases.

### Card Types[¶](https://www.stephenmwangi.com/obsidian-spaced-repetition/flashcards/#card-types "Permanent link")

Stats on card types: New, Young, Mature (Have intervals more than 1 month).

## Intro

A classical bit is represented by 1 or 0. A qubit is represented by what? :: Two numbers describing "how much 0 and how much 1".

We represent a number in a computer with 32 bits. So we need how many bits to represent a qubit? ::64

T/F? When adding qubits, the memory requirement grows exponentially! :: True

What is it good for?
There are some current, small, but measurably better quantum solutions for:
- Designing new materials and drugs through quantum chemistry.
- Optimizing transport and logistics networks via Grover's quantum search algorithm.
- Pricing financial instruments using quantum combinatorial optimization.
- Managing risk in financial portfolios with Quantum Monte Carlo.
- Improved energy efficiency in AI, by encoding huge data sets into quantum states.

T/F? The very first quantum program invented was the Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.::True

DJ algorithm assigns each lottery ticket state a +1 or -1, then adds all the values together "in one step" using quantum interference.

The quantum computer is processing the data in parallel but it can't provide answers for each piece of input data. Instead, it provides a single answer that takes all inputs into account.

Wave patterns are encoded and manipulated in the delicate internal states of quantum things like atoms, molecules, and particles of light. These waves have a size, shape, and location that can be controlled to create any wave shape through interference.

T/F: The first identified real-world application of quantum computers was Shor's algorithm.::True

The key insight Shor had was in translating the math problem of cracking codes into the wave mechanics of quantum computers.

Two examples of post-quantum cryptography are...::lattice-based and hash-based.

Quantum physics is largely about energy at the most fundamental scale. It is here that energy is "quantized" or observed to be discrete. These discrete values of energy are called levels.

The state of lowest possible energy a system can have is called ? All other states the system can be in are called excited states.::ground state.

A "qubit" exists anytime we have at least two states we can measure and manipulate.

Any quantum operation can be implemented using pulses of laster light, microwaves, and RF radiation. We can measure the quantum state of trapped ions using mobile phone cameras!

The notation ∣  ⟩ is called a ?::ket.

In general, for n qubits, there are __ possible computational states.::2^n

In ACID, what does Atomic mean?

Database modifications must follow an "all or nothing" rule.

i.e. No partial transactions.

In CAP Theorem, what does Consistency mean?

Only valid data will be written to the distributed database.
If a transaction is executed that violates the database's consistency rules, the entire transaction is rolled back.

What does Isolation mean?
?
Multiple transactions occurring at the same time don't impact each other's execution.
Transactions will not interfere with each other.

In ACID, what does Durability mean?
?
Any transaction committed to the database will not be lost.
Durability is ensured through the use of database backups and transaction logs that make restoration possible.

What is write-ahead-logging (WAL)?::Write a proposed database transaction to a log first, then execute the transaction.
Any transaction detail is first written to a log that includes both redo and undo information.
If a failure occurs the database can check the log and compare its contents to the state of the database.

What is shadow-paging?

The query's updates are written to the copy, or shadow page, first.
Changes are applied to the database when edits are complete.

REST is an architectural style for ==distributed hypermedia systems.==

Like any other architectural style, REST also has it's own ==6 guiding constraints== (C-SSCLUC) which must be satisfied if an interface is to be considered RESTful.

What are the 6 guiding constraints of REST? (C-SSCLUC)
?
1. Client-server
2. Stateless
3. Cacheable
4. Layered system
5.  Uniform Interface
6. Code on demand (optional)

In REST, what does the client-server principle mean?
?
This essentially means that client application and server application must be able to evolve separately without any dependency on each other.
A client should know only resource URIs and that's all.

What is HATEOAS and why is it important to REST APIs?
?
HATEOAS stands for **Hypertext As The Engine Of Application State.**
It means that hypertext should be used to find your way around the API.
As an example, /account/12345 would return additional links along side account data which would guide the user around the system, like /transfer, /deposit, /close, etc.

In REST, what does Uniform Interface mean?
?
"Once a developer becomes familiar with one of your API, he should be able to follow the similar approach for other APIs."
A resource in the system should have only one logical URI and that should provide a way to fetch related or additional data.
Any single resource should not be too large and contain each and everything in it's representation. Whenever relevant, a resource should contain links pointing to relative URIs (HATEOAS).
Also the resource representations across the system should follow naming conventions, link formats, data formats, etc.
All resources should be accessible through a common approach such as HTTP GET and similarly modified using a consistent approach.

In REST, what does Stateless mean?
?
"No client context shall be stored on the server between requests. The client is responsible for managing the state of the application."
No session, no history.
If the client application needs to be a stateful application for the end-user, then each request from the client should contain all the info necessary to service the request, including auth.

In REST, what does Cacheable mean?
?
"Well managed caching partially or completely eliminates some client-server interactions, further improving scalability and performance."
In REST, caching shall be applied to resources when applicable and then these resources, MUST declare themselves cacheable. Cacheing can be implemented on either the client or server side.

In REST, what does Layered System mean?
?
REST allows you to use a layered system architecture where you deploy the APIs on server A, store data on server B, and authenticate requests on server C.
A client cannot ordinarily tell whether it is connected directly to the end server or an intermediary along the way.

In REST, what does Code on Demand mean?
?
This constraint is optional.
Most of the time you will be sending static representations of resources in form of XML or JSON.
However, you are free to return executable code to support a part of your application.
e.g. clients may call your API to get a UI widget rendering code, it is permitted.

#flashcards

Heads up Vs a small bet..

Check raise more often if:
Low equity draws (gut shots, draws to nut low, back door flush with 2 overs)
Out of position

Why?

Because sometimes the in-position continuation better will just fold.

If they call, you can play the turn based on if your draw improves or not. If it doesn't, just check and defend against small bets. If it does improve, you can continue the betting line and you might be a fold or win a larger pot if you hit the small outer on the river.

Versus a small bet, out of position, low equity draws::Favor raising more often

Call more often if:
High equity draws (Nut flush, open ended with two over cards)

Why?

These hands want to realize equity more often, we're going to hit a monster more often and we want to keep in all their bluffs to allow them to bluff on later streets. We also sometimes will hit marginal top pairs and can bluff catch or play fifth street chicken.

ex [[Don't inflate when drawing in position]]

notes.title: Procrastination
notes.content:
#memex
#flashcards

The first step towards keeping procrastination at bay is to create safety.
?
Failure must not be the end of the world. You need to remember that very successful people had big failures.
*Your value as a person does not depend on the task.*

Channel your energy into actions to remove the threats that you fear.::Fear is the mind killer, fear is the small death.

"I will", "I choose", "I decided"
?
A way to reduce the pressure you feel is to be mindful of language. Avoid “I must” and “I should”. Try to think in terms of positive action words instead of passive desire words.

“I must finish” is not a helpful way of thinking. The better way is “When can I start?”.
?
Try to get things done at least partially, long before a deadline looms.

Partial work is an important aspect: you don't have to complete a big project in one sitting.
?
Bite a small, manageable chunk off and get that done. The project may be big, but it can be tackled in smaller parts. Do a first draft. Or one test chapter. Maybe it even helps to do a first draft sloppily on purpose and edit it afterwards.

“I must be perfect” is inhumane.
?
You are allowed to be human. Learn from mistakes, respect boundaries. Don't criticise yourself harshly. Have some compassion for yourself.

Schedule time off.
?
Friends, Leisure time, your partner. They are important and healthy for you. Incorporate leisure time and sports into your schedule. Don't let it be a secondary concern for “when you find the time”.
Think “unschedule” where you plan your fun first.

Imagine the concrete goal and the rewards.
?
Let it pull you towards it. Don't think about the long way till the goal, think about the way you've already behind yourself.

Don't get overwhelmed.
?
You don't have to know the perfect starting point. You may take time to learn and feel secure in your task. Don't bad-mouth your achievements and progress.

Plan in reverse and invent lots of smaller deadlines.
?
Start with the externally imposed deadline. Plan backwards what needs to be done to complete the task by that time. Plan intermediate steps with their own, much shorter deadlines.

Sometimes people work on tasks pretty well and productively, but they never seem to finish a task.
?
Prolonging the almost-finished task takes up energy, as well. Just put that energy into finishing and reap the rewards.

Don't be discouraged by the seeming lack of progress after starting.
?
It's often the case that the beginning is the hardest and slowest part. The time spent in the first phase isn't lost, you've got a better understanding of the problem and your task.

The fear that the demands of you will rise after successfully finishing the current job is irrational.
?
You will still have some autonomy to make an informed decision later. Don't fret about it now.

If you feel that you need more time: are you sure that it isn't just perfectionism?
?
Not everything needs to be polished. Weigh the cost and benefit of working on it some more versus finishing it.

Use the "unschedule".
?
The Unschedule is like a schedule, but it starts with you entering blocks of recreational activities and leisure time. Only then do you enter your tasks, after you've worked at least half an hour without interruption on them. This gives you a realistic overview of how much work you can possibly tackle. Tasks are never scheduled, only recorded after the fact.

Aim for fifty five minutes of uninterrupted, quality work.
?
Take a break after that block.

A good way to start on managing procrastination is having a procrastination log.
?
Jot down the time, the activity, your thoughts and feelings, your excuse, your attempt of a solution and your resulting thoughts and feelings.

Procrastination is a mechanism to cope with the fear that is linked to the beginning or the end of a task.
?
Nobody is “lazy” on all fields of endeavor. You might not be able to start the next chapter of your novel, but still do the required reading for your college course.

The usual cycle of procrastination looks like this:
?
1. You let the task at hand influence your happiness and self-worth.
2. You want to execute the task very well to satisfy your perfectionism. Thereby you increase your chance of failure by setting the bar very high.
3. You fear that you cannot meet the expectations you have imposed on yourself. You cannot act.
4. You avoid the problem by procrastinating.
5. Shortly before the deadline you _have_ to do something. Given the time allotted, you do it, but not as well as you could have.
6. You tell yourself it's acceptable you couldn't do any better because you didn't have enough time.

Excessive preparation before beginning a task is also just procrastination.
?
Limit prep time then just start.
If you really need research or other preparation, you will find out later.

Drop goals that can neither be achieved nor started upon in the near future.
?
Change your plans and re-schedule it for a later time. Don't let that goal linger without any action towards completion.

I wish I hadn't worked so hard.
?
This came from every male patient that I nursed. They missed their children's youth and their partner's companionship. Women also spoke of this regret, but as most were from an older generation, many of the female patients had not been breadwinners. All of the men I nursed deeply regretted spending so much of their lives on the treadmill of a work existence.

I wish I'd had the courage to live a life true to myself, not the life others expected of me.
?
This was the most common regret of all. When people realize that their life is almost over and look back clearly on it, it is easy to see how many dreams have gone unfulfilled. Most people had not honored even a half of their dreams and had to die knowing that it was due to choices they had made, or not made. Health brings a freedom very few realize, until they no longer have it.

I wish I'd had the courage to express my feelings.
?
Many people suppressed their feelings in order to keep peace with others. As a result, they settled for a mediocre existence and never became who they were truly capable of becoming. Many developed illnesses relating to the bitterness and resentment they carried as a result.

I wish I'd stayed in touch with my friends.
?
Often they would not truly realize the full benefits of old friends until their dying weeks and it was not always possible to track them down. Many had become so caught up in their own lives that they had let golden friendships slip by over the years. There were many deep regrets about not giving friendships the time and effort that they deserved. Everyone misses their friends when they are dying.

I wish that I had let myself be happier.
?
This is a surprisingly common one. Many did not realize until the end that happiness is a choice. They had stayed stuck in old patterns and habits. The so-called 'comfort' of familiarity overflowed into their emotions, as well as their physical lives. Fear of change had them pretending to others, and to their selves, that they were content, when deep within, they longed to laugh properly and have silliness in their life again.
